drivingQuestion: Why does R' Shimon need to say 'to what is this similar'?

segments.he: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם מִקְצָת אַמּוֹתָיו שֶׁל זֶה וְכוּ׳. לְמָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר ״לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה״?
segments.en: The mishna taught: «If there were two» people positioned in a way that «part of the» four «cubits of the one» were subsumed within the four cubits of the other, they each may bring food and eat together in the shared area in the middle. Rabbi Shimon likened this case to that of three courtyards that open one into another, where the two outer courtyards established an eiruv with the middle one. The Gemara asks: «Why does» Rabbi Shimon «need to» offer an analogy and «say: To what may this be likened,» and thus connect our case to a different issue?
